headline: Taboo Sprint Activity — Forbidden Words Speaking Game for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students rapidly expand active vocabulary by finding synonyms, definitions, and circumlocutions under pressure
Build speaking fluency and spontaneity — students must communicate without their usual go-to words
Develop listening comprehension as students decode descriptions without the expected keyword
Practise the real-world skill of explaining meaning when a word is unknown — essential for fluent communication
howItWorks: The AI generates a target word and four forbidden words related to it — all shown on the teacher's screen
One student describes the target word to their team without using any of the five forbidden words
Team members guess the word on their devices while the teacher monitors for violations with a buzz button
Rounds are timed — the team scores for each correct guess, with bonus points for speed
teacherUseCases: Vocabulary production practice — students move from passive recognition to active, flexible use of words
Speaking fluency drill — the time pressure and forbidden words force students to speak without pausing to translate
Review lesson — run Taboo Sprint at the end of a unit to surface which words students can explain vs which they just recognise

faq.q: How are the forbidden words chosen?
faq.a: The AI selects the four most natural helper words for the target — the words students would normally reach for first. Banning them forces creative circumlocution. For example, for 'migration', the AI might forbid: move, country, travel, birds.

Using a forbidden word, the target word itself, or any part of it (e.g. saying 'migrate' when 'migration' is the target). The teacher controls the buzz button and is the final judge — there's no automated detection.

faq.q: Can shy or lower-level students participate?
faq.a: Yes. Lower-difficulty settings produce simpler target words and more obvious circumlocutions. You can also let students pass a round if they're stuck — the game supports skipping to the next word without a penalty.

faq.q: How many rounds does a session typically cover?
faq.a: A 20-minute session typically covers 6–10 words depending on the pace of guessing. The AI generates a full set of words upfront so there's no loading delay between rounds.

faq.q: Does the whole class play at once or do teams compete?
faq.a: The standard mode is team-based — one speaker per round, team guesses together. For smaller groups, the whole class can guess simultaneously. The teacher controls when to advance to the next word.

faq.q: Is Taboo Sprint free to use?
faq.a: Yes, Taboo Sprint is free. Students join on any phone or tablet through a shared browser link — no download or student account required.
